channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seeks to Prohibit Foreign Control Over Satellite Networks
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to ban foreign entities from controlling its satellite networks. This move aims to assert national sovereignty and control over critical communication infrastructure. The specific details of the proposed legislation and its implications are yet to be fully disclosed.

item.title: Second Crushing and Transfer Complex Launched at Bolashak Mine in Kazakhstan
item.description: A second crushing and transfer complex has been commissioned at the Bolashak mine of Donskoy GOK in Kazakhstan. The new facility will increase the capacity of the underground transport system and improve operational efficiency and safety. This upgrade is part of a larger infrastructure development plan for the mine.

item.title: Bishkek Marks 85th Anniversary of the Feat of the 28 Panfilov Guardsmen
item.description: Bishkek hosted the opening of the historical-documentary exhibition "Our Panfilov" to commemorate the 85th anniversary of the feat of the 28 Panfilov guardsmen. The event showcased historical exhibits belonging to the Panfilov division, attended by military personnel, students, and public representatives.

item.title: Osh Allocates 10 Hectares of Agricultural Land for Residential and Administrative Buildings
item.description: Osh has reclassified 10.22 hectares of irrigated arable land for the construction of multi-story buildings and administrative facilities. The decision, signed by the Cabinet of Ministers chairman, involves four land plots. Compensation for the converted land is required within three years.

item.title: US President Trump Begins Asia Trip for Historic Summit with Putin and Xi
item.description: US President Donald Trump has embarked on a multi-day trip to Asia for a historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The summit in Shenzhen, China, will focus on nuclear arms control and the war in Iran. Trump may also meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

item.title: US Preparing for Next Round of Ukraine Peace Negotiations
item.description: The US is preparing for the next round of negotiations on a Ukrainian settlement, according to Jared Kushner. Representatives from the US, Russia, and Ukraine have held talks, with further discussions planned. The EU is proposing Europe as a venue for future talks.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Bank Deposits Grow by 794 Billion Tenge in October
item.description: In October 2026, Kazakhstani bank deposits increased by 794 billion tenge, reaching 29.4 trillion tenge. The growth was primarily in tenge deposits, with foreign currency deposits falling to 14% of the total. This marks the second-largest monthly increase of the year.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Approves Land Use and Spatial Development Concept Until 2050
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has approved the Concept for Rational Land Use and Spatial Development of Kyrgyzstan until 2050. The document aims to foster sustainable territorial development, efficient use of land and water resources, preserve agricultural potential, and enhance food, water, and infrastructure security.

item.title: Singapore Doubles Trade with Kazakhstan, Reaching $1.5 Billion in Nine Months
item.description: Kazakhstan's trade with Singapore surged by 2.3 times in January-September 2026, reaching $1.5 billion. Exports, primarily oil, grew 2.5 times to $1.4 billion. New exports include nickel profiles and zinc powder. Imports from Singapore decreased by 9.4% to $62.3 million, though computer and oil imports increased.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Institute of Balneology Transferred to Presidential Affairs Administration
item.description: The Kyrgyz Scientific Research Institute of Balneology and Restorative Treatment is being transferred from the Ministry of Health to the Presidential Affairs Administration. This decision aims to improve state institution management and optimize sanatorium-resort and rehabilitation activities. The institute will retain its current staff, payment conditions, and assets.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Meets Sultan of Oman to Boost Bilateral Relations
item.description: Uzbekistan's President met with the Sultan of Oman, emphasizing that the visit will serve the interests of both nations. The leaders expressed confidence that the visit marks a significant step in elevating bilateral relations. Relations between Uzbekistan and Oman have been actively developing, with strengthened political dialogue and expanding trade, economic, and cultural ties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Leads EAEU in Construction Growth, But Housing Starts Lag
item.description: Kyrgyzstan recorded the highest construction growth rate in the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) at 82.9% in January-September 2026, according to the Eurasian Economic Commission. However, housing starts increased by only 1% during the same period, significantly lagging behind other EAEU members. The discrepancy between overall construction volume and housing completion remains unexplained.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Appoints New Representatives to the Venice Commission
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has appointed new representatives for Kyrgyzstan to the European Commission for Democracy through Law, commonly known as the Venice Commission. Justice Minister Almaz Ayilchiev will serve as the representative, with the Deputy Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, Jyldyz Taalaibek kyzy, as his deputy. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is tasked with implementing the necessary measures following the new decree.

item.title: Kazakh Stewardess Hospitalized in Kuwait with Mysterious Illness After Nepal Flight
item.description: A 25-year-old Kazakhstani flight attendant was hospitalized in intensive care in Kuwait following a flight from Nepal. The cause of her sudden deterioration remains undiagnosed, with doctors investigating several potential illnesses. Kazakh diplomats are providing consular assistance and maintaining contact with her family and medical staff.

item.title: Goldman Sachs Lowers Gold Price Forecast for End of 2027
item.description: Goldman Sachs has reduced its year-end 2027 gold price forecast from $4,800 to $4,650 per troy ounce. Analysts cite expectations of further US interest rate hikes, which could diminish private investor interest in the precious metal. The bank anticipates the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December 2026 and March 2027.

item.title: Magnitude 7.1 Earthquake Strikes Indonesia's Maluku Province
item.description: A powerful 7.1 magnitude earthquake has been recorded in the island region of Indonesia's Maluku province. The epicenter was located southwest of Aru Island. The tremors were felt in some parts of Indonesia, but no casualties or damage have been reported. A tsunami warning has been ruled out.

item.title: Head of Aktobe gas station network shot dead at home, robbed of car and valuables
item.description: The head of a gas station network in Aktobe, 49-year-old Aybolat Zhissov, was shot dead in his home. An unknown assailant broke into the businessman's house, shot him, and then fled with money, valuables, and his car. Police have opened a criminal case for murder and are conducting an investigation to identify and apprehend the suspect.

item.title: Nearly 500 Employees in Tajikistan Punished for Electricity Theft and Falsification
item.description: In Tajikistan, approximately 500 employees of the 'Electric Distribution Networks' were penalized for illegally adding over 168.8 million kWh of electricity to consumer bills, causing a loss of about 51.3 million somoni. 400 employees faced administrative penalties, while criminal cases were initiated against 89 others.

item.title: China Hosts APEC 2026, Focusing on Opportunities Amidst Global Uncertainty
item.description: China presides over APEC in 2026, with the theme 'Building an Asia-Pacific Community for Shared Prosperity.' The forum prioritizes openness, innovation, and cooperation to navigate challenges like protectionism and supply chain shifts. Efforts focus on market access and regulatory harmonization.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Rules for Tracking School Absences and Bullying
item.description: From November 21, 2026, Kazakhstan will implement updated rules for monitoring children and preventing school bullying. A unified digital registry will track absences, and bullying response times will be reduced to one day. A database for children aged 0-18 will be created, including information on systematic unexcused absences.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Leaders Award Each Other Medals
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev began a two-day state visit to Oman. He was met by Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said. High-level talks were held at the 'Al-Alam' palace, focusing on bilateral cooperation and regional/international issues. Business delegation meetings also took place.

item.title: Five EU Countries Agree to Deport Migrants to Rwanda
item.description: Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, Austria, and Greece will soon open a migrant detention center in Rwanda for individuals to be deported from the EU. The center, set to open in 2027, will house irregular migrants who will be offered the right to live, study, and work in Rwanda. Human rights groups have criticized the plan, citing Rwanda's human rights record.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Leaders Exchange High State Awards
item.description: The Presidents of Uzbekistan and Oman, Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Haitham bin Tarik Al Said, were awarded each other's highest state honors in Muscat. The awards signify a commitment to strengthening bilateral friendship and advancing multifaceted cooperation between the two nations.

item.title: US Envoy: Trump Aims to Prevent Nuclear Armageddon, Discuss Arms Control
item.description: US Permanent Representative to NATO, Matthew Whitaker, stated that President Donald Trump intends to prevent "nuclear armageddon." Whitaker commented on upcoming meetings between Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping, emphasizing the need for global nuclear stability. The leaders are expected to discuss nuclear arms reduction and the war with Iran.

item.title: President of Uzbekistan Meets with Leaders of Leading Omani Companies
item.description: During a state visit to the Sultanate of Oman, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan met with representatives of major Omani businesses. Discussions focused on increasing the charter capital of the Uzbek-Omani Investment Company and implementing joint projects in mining, electrical engineering, green energy, and logistics.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deputy PM Demands Winter Flood Preparedness Before Winter Arrives
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev chaired a meeting on regional readiness for winter and spring flood season. He stressed the need to complete all major preparatory work before winter, citing snow clearing and flood risk in over 1,200 settlements. Specific attention was given to four regions requiring further flood control measures.

item.title: Official Welcome Ceremony Held for Uzbekistan President in Oman
item.description: An official welcome ceremony for Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev took place at the Al-Alam Palace in Muscat, Oman, during his state visit. A horse-mounted honor guard greeted the President, followed by a 21-gun salute. The leaders then proceeded to a high-level meeting after the ceremony concluded.

item.title: 38 Countries Warn of Nuclear Accident Risk in Ukraine Due to Attacks
item.description: Regulators from 38 countries have expressed concern over attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, warning of a potential nuclear accident. They urged an end to attacks on facilities ensuring the safe operation of nuclear power plants. Experts noted that power outages could lead to reactor core meltdowns and radioactive release, comparable to Chernobyl.

item.title: Uzbekistan and US Develop Investment Cooperation in Oil and Gas
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing investment cooperation in its oil and gas sector with US financial institutions, including Citi Bank. Discussions focused on strengthening mutually beneficial partnerships, with presentations on the company's financial status, production, exploration, and modernization projects. Citi Bank, established in 1812, is a major international financial institution.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Football Team Coach's Future Uncertain After Nations League
item.description: John van 't Schip, head coach of the Kazakhstan national football team, has not made a definitive decision about his future with the team following the conclusion of the Nations League. He stated his primary task was to manage the Nations League games, which has now been completed. The team finished last in their group with three draws and three losses.

item.title: Central Asia's Trade and Investment with Gulf States See Significant Growth
item.description: Trade between Central Asia and Gulf states has nearly quadrupled between 2020 and 2025, reaching $3.9 billion. Gulf investment in the region also tripled, exceeding $31.1 billion by mid-2026, with power generation being a key sector. High transportation costs are expected to slow future trade expansion.

item.title: Former Afghan Security Officer Killed by Unidentified Gunmen in Pakistan's Balochistan
item.description: Sharifullah, a former local police commander from Afghanistan's Ghazni Province, was killed by unidentified gunmen in the Sarwanan market in Pakistan's Balochistan province. He had fled to Iran after the Taliban takeover and later moved to Pakistan after an attack there. No group has claimed responsibility.

item.title: Turkmenistan Approves Composition of Turkmen Side of Intergovernmental Committee with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: To further develop cooperation between Turkmenistan and the Kyrgyz Republic, the President of Turkmenistan signed a decree. The decree approves the composition of the Turkmen side of the intergovernmental committee on trade-economic, scientific-technical, and humanitarian cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allows Officials to Earn Additional Income
item.description: Officials in Kyrgyzstan are now permitted to engage in additional paid work in education, science, and other professional fields, provided they obtain management approval. This work must not interfere with their primary official duties. The new regulation aims to allow for supplementary earnings.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Replaces Yemen Coalition Commander Amid Houthi Advances
item.description: Saudi Arabia has replaced its military coalition commander in Yemen following significant battlefield setbacks. General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili now leads the joint forces, replacing Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman, who becomes an adviser to the defense minister. These changes are linked to the deteriorating military situation as Houthi fighters advance towards Aden.

item.title: 120 Afghan Women Urge French President to Expedite Asylum Applications
item.description: One hundred twenty Afghan women in Iran and Pakistan have appealed to French President Emmanuel Macron to increase humanitarian visa quotas and speed up asylum processing. They fear deportation to Afghanistan due to past activities. The group includes activists, journalists, and former military officers.

item.title: South Korea Donates $6 Million for Afghan Returnees and Affected Communities
item.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has launched a $6 million project funded by South Korea to support returnees, displaced persons, and victims of natural disasters in five Afghan provinces. The 'REVIVE Plus' project focuses on infrastructure reconstruction, livelihood recovery, and improving basic services, aiming to benefit over 386,000 people directly and indirectly.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Awarded Oman's Highest State Decoration
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has been honored with Oman's highest state award, the 'Al-Said' Order. In a reciprocal gesture, the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, was presented with the Uzbek 'Order of Friendship' of the highest degree. This exchange highlights the strong diplomatic ties between the two nations.

item.title: FAO Provides Financial Support to Agricultural Businesses in Nine Afghan Provinces
item.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is offering cash assistance to agricultural businesses and related industries in nine Afghan provinces. Funded by the Asian Development Bank, the initiative aims to strengthen food security and health services, with grants ranging from $5,000 to $15,000.

item.title: Man Arrested in Qashqadaryo for Promising to Sell 36 Hectares of Land
item.description: A man has been arrested in Qashqadaryo for allegedly promising to sell 36 hectares of land for $18,500. The individual reportedly agreed to transfer the land, leased for 49 years, to another person through his contacts in the local administration.
